val: ual (fel) — as; conjunction, spelt val (Ac val y bydynt 'and as they were')
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth) · also yd 'corn, grain' noun m. (y diua dy yd 'to destroy your corn')
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
wydyon: Gwydion — personal name (Gwydyon, Wydyon); soft-mutated (G>w) after gan 'with', after e 'to' and in apposition to ynteu (Ynteu Wydyon 'he, Gwydion')
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying') · also 'into' with rithyaw (eu rithyaw yn llygot 'to change them into mice') · yn ol 'after' (yn ol guyr y Deheu 'after the men of the South'); yn + predicate with verbs of becoming, 'into, as' (yny uyd yn garw 'until he becomes a stag'; yn uab braswineu telediw 'into a boy'); yn y lle 'at once'; yn y taraw wynteu 'in their striking', striking them (y here for eu 'their', yn 'in')
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that') · also (13) for predicative yn 'as', with soft mutation (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach) · (14) y ar 'from off' (y ar seith cantref Dyuet 'from off the seven cantrefs of Dyfed') · also y 'its, his' before a verbal noun, standing for the noun's object and softening it (na'y werthu 'nor selling it'; na'y ollwng 'nor releasing it') · y hediw 'from today' (a blwydyn y hediw 'and a year from today'); y 'to' before a verbal noun of purpose (lle idaw y benelinyaw 'a place for him to recline'); y 'his' twice in ar y bwyt a'y llynn 'on his food and his drink'
wely: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. present 'you will see', soft-mutated after a (ti a wely a wneuthum i yrot ti) · also in the presentative (a) wely di 'do you see?' = 'behold' (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son'; the Red Book has weldy), softened after the question particle a, which is absorbed · gwely (gwely) — bed; noun m., g lost by soft mutation after 'th 'your' and y 'his' (i'th wely 'in your bed'; traed y wely 'the feet of his bed')
ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done') · y gyt ac y + verb, 'as soon as' (y gyt ac y bedydywyt 'as soon as he was baptised'; y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'as soon as he came to the sea')
deffroi: deffroi (deffro) — to wake, awaken; verbal noun (thu a'r pylgeint deffroi 'towards dawn, to wake'); no mutation
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall') · also (10) linking a fronted adjective to its noun, with soft mutation of the noun (ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'); here a is not the conjunction
glywei: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after a (ef a glywei llef erchwys arall 'he heard the cry of another pack')
diaspat: diasbad (diasbad) — cry, shout, outcry; noun m. (dodi diaspat uchel 'to give a loud cry'); radical as object of dodi
gist: kist (cist) — chest; noun f. (ymywn llaw gist 'inside a hand-chest', a small chest); soft-mutated (k>g) as the second element of the compound llaw gist
is: is (is) — below, under; preposition (is dy draet 'under your feet'; is traed y wely 'under the feet of his bed'); no mutation
draet: troet (troed) — foot; plural traet (traed), soft-mutated (t > d) after y 'his' (am y draet 'on his feet') · also soft after dy 'your' (is dy draet 'under your feet')
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
uchel: uchel (uchel) — high; adjective (ar garrec uchel 'on a high rock'); no mutation (vowel) · also 'loud' of a sound (dodi diaspat uchel 'giving a loud cry')
hi: hi — 'she, her'; independent 3 sg. f. pronoun
kyuuch: kyuuch (cyfuwch) — as high as; equative of uchel 'high' (kyuuch a chrib yr ystauell 'as high as the ridge of the chamber'); no mutation
kigleu: klywet (clywed) — to hear; old 3 sg. preterite 'heard' (a phawb o'r guyrda a'e kigleu 'and every one of the noblemen heard it'); no mutation after a'e 'it'
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
oruc: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite auxiliary 'he did', soft-mutated after a, with g dropped (kyuodi a oruc)
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
kyuodi: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; verbal noun (kyuodi a oruc 'he rose')
gyflym: kyflym (cyflym) — swift; adjective, soft-mutated (k>g) after yn (yn gyflym caeu y got 'quickly shutting the bag') · also soft-mutated (k>g) after y in an adverbial phrase (y gyflym 'quickly')
agori: agori (agor) — to open; verbal noun (Agori y drws a oruc ef 'he opened the door'); no mutation
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
welei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect 'he saw' (welei), soft-mutated after a (ef a welei lannerch) · also 'would see' (neu ynteu a welei rywedawt 'or else he would see a wonder')
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God')
bychan: bychan (bychan) — small, little, slight; adjective (bychan a dial oed 'it would be a small revenge'); no mutation
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
llen: llen (llen) — cloth, mantle, covering; noun f. (Llen o bali 'a cloth of brocade'); no mutation
gymerth: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 sg. preterite 'took', soft-mutated after a (Y march a gymerth 'he took the horse'; a gymerth rygyng 'took an amble')
mab: mab (mab) — son, boy; noun m. (mab a anet idaw 'a son was born to him'); no mutation (subject, fronted)
rwng: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, base uninflected form
dwylaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., dual/plural dwylaw 'hands', from dwy llaw 'two hands' (a'y dwylaw 'and her hands'); no mutation
gyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after y (y gyrchwys 'he made for') · also soft-mutated after the relative particle a with the object fronted (y gaer a gyrchwys ef 'the fort he made for') · also soft after a with the subject fronted (Enteu Math a gyrchwys Caer Tathyl 'and Math made for Caer Dathyl'; y mor a gyrchwys 'he made for the sea')
dref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f., soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (ar y dref 'on the town') · also soft after holl (yn yr holl dref 'in the whole town') and after y 'to' (y dref arall 'to another town')
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form · yn y lle 'at once, on the spot' (Ac yn y lle, y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'and at once, as soon as he came to the sea'); lle idaw y benelinyaw 'a place for him to recline'
bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...') · also introducing a reported fact, 'that (it) was' (adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu 'knowing that their gain was failing'; clybot bot y gwyr 'hearing that the men were')
gwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., meaning as context decides (a'y wreic 'and his wife')
genti: gan (gan) — 'with her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f., spelt genti (a chanawon genti 'and whelps with her'); no mutation
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
wreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., soft-mutated after a'y/possessive (ymdidan a'y wreic) · also soft after the article, as a feminine noun (y wreic 'the woman') · also soft after predicative yn (yn wreic 'as wife') and as the subject straight after a verb (ny bu wreic delediwach 'there was no comelier woman')
ueithryn: meithryn (meithrin) — to foster, rear; verbal noun (am ueithryn y mab 'for fostering the boy'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition am · also soft after y 'his', standing for the object (ac a baraf y ueithryn 'and I will have him fostered')
ulwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., soft-mutated after y/the feminine article (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn) · also adverbial, 'a year' in time phrases, soft-mutated without the article (ulwydyn y heno 'a year from tonight'; ual yd eistedyssant ulwydyn o'r nos honno 'as they sat a year from that night'), the soft mutation being that of an adverbial accusative of time · also soft after a preceding ordinal (y seithuet ulwydyn 'the seventh year')
oet: oet (oed) — appointed time, tryst; noun m. (y mae oet y rof i ac ef 'there is an appointment between me and him') · also a spelling of oed 'was', 3 sg. imperfect of bot (yn yd oet Pwyll 'where Pwyll was') · also 'time of life, age' (a breisc oed yn yr oet oed arnaw 'and big he was for his age')
gantunt: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'with them' (a'r gennadwri honno gantunt 'with that message with them')
ureisket: breisc (breisg) — stout, bulky; equative ureisket 'as stout as' (kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six years'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the equative cyn
dwy: dwy (dwy) — two (f.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following feminine noun (y dwy dyrnas 'the two kingdoms')
ulwyd: blwyd (blwydd) — year (of age); noun f. (yny oed ulwyd 'until he was a year old'; cynn y ulwyd 'before his first year'); soft-mutated (b>u) as the predicate directly after oed, and after the possessive y 'his'
eil: eil (ail) — second; ordinal numeral (yr eil 'the second') · also in the name Dylan Eil Ton, eil 'second' or 'son, offspring' (sense of the epithet disputed)
mawr: mawr (mawr) — big, great; adjective (uarch erchlas mawr 'a big dapple-grey horse')
gallu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m. (herwyd uyg gallu i 'according to my power'); nasal-mutated (g>ng) after uy 'my', written uyg gallu with the g on the possessive
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also in e hun (ehun) 'self, own', unchanged for any person (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'; synnyaw e hun 'watching for himself') · also the y of y rof 'between me' in the oath (E rof a Duw 'between me and God') · also 'his' before a vowel and before h (e ystauell 'his chamber'; e hutlath 'his magic rod')
hun: hun (hun) — self, own; also 'sleep' as a separate noun by context (e hunan/e hun 'himself'; kymryt hun 'to take sleep')
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
uwy: mwy (mwy) — more, greater; comparative, soft-mutated after a noun or a (ansyberwyt uwy; a uei uwy no hynny)
noc: no (na) — than; spelling before a vowel (noc a uu 'than what was')
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
dyn: dyn (dyn) — man, person; noun m. (y dyn eithaf 'the farthest man')
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
magwyt: magu (magu) — to rear, bring up; impersonal preterite 'was reared' (y magwyt y mab 'the boy was reared'), -wyt; no mutation after the particle y
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them') · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny uu damunet gantunt 'until there was desire in them') and as after the relative a left unwritten (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man') · also 'she was' after a fronted predicate, the relative a understood (a lleidyr uu hi arnaf i 'and a thief she was against me') · also an apparent slip for uy (fy) 'my' in mi uu hun 'I myself' (the Red Book has miui uy hun)
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing') · also soft after dy 'your' (dy uot yn kyuanhedu 'your being settled')
gerdawd: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel, go; 3 sg. preterite 'went', soft-mutated (c>g) after a (Gwawl a gerdawd ryngthaw a'y gyuoeth 'Gwawl went his way to his realm')
ol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m. (yn ol y cwn 'after the hounds'; yn y ol 'in its track')
gwydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (Gwydyon); radical (the y before it in heb y Gwydyon is the particle that introduces a named speaker)
orymdeith: gorymdeith (gorymdaith) — walking about, a progress; noun f., used after y 'to' like a verbal noun ('to walk about'); g lost by soft mutation after y 'to' (kyuodi y orymdeith 'rising to walk about')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
caer: caer (caer) — fortress, walled court; noun f.; first element of the place-name Caer Tathyl, Math's court (Caer Dathyl); radical as object after a gyrchwys
aranrot: Aranrot (Arianrhod) — personal name, Gwydion's sister, daughter of Don (Aranrot uerch Don 'Aranrhod daughter of Don'); radical
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them') · y gyt ac y + verb 'as soon as' (y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'as soon as he came to the sea'); y gyt without a, 'together, as one' (ywch gerdet y gyt 'you to go together'); y gyt a chwi 'with you'
gwedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, the spelling beside guedy (A gwedy y bwyta kyntaf 'and after the first eating')
erbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — (1) against, by (a time) (erbyn hanner dyd 'by midday'); (2) 'to meet' (yn y erbyn 'to meet him')
guell: guell (gwell) — better; comparative adjective, in kyuarch guell 'greet' (literally 'ask better') · also the plain comparative 'better' (guell eu kic no chic eidon 'their flesh is better than beef'; ae guell 'is it better')
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
ro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give', in a wish after the particle a; r- shows no mutation (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good')
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay')
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
di: di — 'you' (sg.), echoing pronoun after a verb or possessive (y pryny di; dy gerennyd di); also the object 'you' (ni ladaf i di)
hwnn: hwnn (hwn) — 'this' (m.); demonstrative (yr oet hwnn 'this appointment') · also pronoun 'the one that' (namyn yr hwnn a dyly 'but that which it deserves')
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
wr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ansyberwyt uwy ar wr) · also soft after y 'to' (y wr 'to a man, to a husband') · also soft in address (A wr 'O man') and after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw wr 'what kind of man') · also subject directly after a negated verb, soft-mutated (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come') · also soft after at 'to' (at wr mawr 'to a great man')
ba: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, a variant spelling with b (Ba ryw leidyr 'what kind of thief'; cf. byhyt for py hyt); whether b is a mutation here is uncertain; causes soft mutation of a following noun
doi: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. imperfect 'used to come, came' (kystal y doi y gof 'as well came to mind')
arnat: ar — conjugated preposition 'on you' (sg.) (y mae arnat o anryded 'there is rank on you'; a'm ansawd arnat ti)
uyg: uy (fy) — my; possessive, here spelt uyg before k-: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation the noun would take (uyg kyuoeth = fy nghyfoeth 'my realm')
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you') · also echoing a possessive (wy gwreic i yw hi 'she is my wife')
dilyt: dilyt (dilyn) — to follow, pursue, keep on with; verbal noun (no dilyt kyuedach 'than to pursue carousing'); no mutation
kywilyd: cywilydd (cywilydd) — shame, disgrace; noun m. (Vyg kywilyd 'my shame', object fronted); written radical, the nasal mutation shown only in vyg
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs') · also yr hynn 'that which, what' (yr hynn a deryw ymi 'what befalls me')
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise') · also with soft mutation of g (ony wybydaf i 'if I do not find out') · also 'if not' with the subjunctive (ony bei hagyr 'if it were not unseemly')
byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag') · also byt 'world', spelt with d (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the world's host of mice'; the Red Book y byt)
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach) · also in kyn no hynny 'before that, earlier than that'

dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')

gauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find, reach; 3 sg. preterite 'got', soft-mutated after a (a gauas 'got, reached')
digawn: digawn (digon) — enough, sufficient; adjective/noun (Digawn ry dodet ymman 'enough has been put here'; digawn yw hynny 'that is enough')
difflannu: diflannu (diflannu) — to vanish, disappear; verbal noun, written with ff (difflannu y gaer 'the fort vanishing'); no mutation
gueith: gweith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, the thing made; noun m., gu- spells gw- (o'r gueith hwnnw 'of that work'; y gueith wynteu 'their work'); radical after the article and after y standing for eu 'their'
hwy: hwy (hwy) — 'they, them'; independent 3 pl. pronoun (arnunt hwy 'over them') · also 'longer', comparative of hir (Ny bu hwy ganthunt no thrannoeth 'it was no longer with them than the next day')
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why') · also in o achaws 'because of' (o achaws y carchar hwnnw 'because of that prison')
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
gelwit: galw (galw) — to call; 3 sg. impersonal imperfect 'he was called' (y gelwit Pwyll Penn Annwuyn)
drydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ymgueiraw a oruc Teirnon ar y drydyd marchawc 'Teirnon made ready as third rider'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his'
gryd: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker, cobbler; noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'from' (gan gryd 'from a shoemaker')
well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land') · also soft as the predicate straight after the verb (nat oed well genti 'it was no better to her') · also na well 'no, not better', reply 'Na well' (soft-mutated gw>w after na)
wrthyf: wrth (wrth) + i — conjugated preposition 'to/at me' (na dywedy di wrthyf i)
buum: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. preterite 'I was' (ny buum distaw 'I was not silent'); b unmutated after ny
wrthyt: wrth (wrth) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to/at you' (Dywedaf wrthyt; chadw kywirdeb wrthyt titheu)
bryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent, purpose, mood; noun m., t for d (ac y bryt ar eu dienydyaw 'and their mind on putting them to death', the y being eu 'their'); radical · also bryt ← pryt 'form, looks', soft-mutated (p>b) after dy 'your' (colli dy bryt a'th liw 'losing your looks and your colour'); a different word from bryt 'mind'
kymerth: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; old 3 sg. preterite without -wys ending (y kymerth ynteu y furuf e hun)
furyf: ffuryf (ffurf) — form, manner; noun f., variant spelling of furuf; ff does not mutate, the single f is the scribe's spelling (pa furyf 'in what manner')
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
arueu: arueu (arfau) — arms, armour; noun pl. (yny dyrr yr arueu oll 'so that all the armour breaks')
ymdanaw: am (am) + ef — 'about him/it'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt ymdanaw (amouyn yn lut ymdanaw 'inquiring secretly about it'); no mutation
rof: rwng (rhwng) + i — conjugated preposition 'between me' (y rof i a Duw 'between me and God')
geif: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. present 'will get', soft-mutated (c>g) after a (Ef a geif hynny 'he will get that')
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
dinas: dinas (dinas) — city, fortified town; noun f. (kyrchu dinas arall 'making for another city'); radical as object after the verbal noun
pob: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective (pob un 'each one')
march: march (march) — horse; noun m., base form (y march 'the horse')
gwbyl: cwbyl (cwbl) — whole, complete; adjective; soft-mutated (c>g) as the predicate after uu (yny uu gwbyl idaw y dal 'until his payment was complete to him') · also soft-mutated (c>g) as object after ry geueist (neu ry geueist gwbyl 'you have got the whole')
meint: maint (maint) — size, amount, extent; noun, spelt meint; y meint goruot 'so much victory, the whole measure of victory'; radical
adnabot: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; verbal noun (adnabot meithryn yr ederyn 'recognising the nursing of the bird')
kymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun (iawn yw gymryt; kymryt gwrogaeth)
dihirwch: dihirwch (dihirwch) — wretchedness, misery, worthlessness; noun m. (yn y dihirwch hwnn 'in this wretchedness'); no mutation after the article
eisseu: eisseu (eisiau) — lack, absence, want; noun m. (i eisseu ef 'his absence')
meirch: march (march) — horse; noun pl. (meirch a milgwn 'horses and greyhounds')
was: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant; noun m., soft-mutated in address (Ha was 'ho, lad'; Bid parawt … was 'be ready, lad') and after wrth (wrth was y uarch 'to his groom', literally 'the lad of his horse') · also soft after predicative yn (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
awn: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. 'let us go' (Awn parth a'r llys 'let us go towards the court') or 'we will go' (ni a awn)
ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also the softened pronoun 'I' after a verb (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot bring myself to do what you say') and as the second, emphatic pronoun in mi ui 'I myself' (A mi ui a rodaf 'and I myself will give'); soft-mutated from mi · also after gwae 'woe' (guae ui 'woe is me')
thi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and, with' (gyt a thi 'together with you')
neges: neges (neges) — errand, business; noun f. (yd oed neges idi 'she had an errand'; Pennaf neges 'the chief errand')
auory: auory (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (o'r dyd auory 'from the day tomorrow')
wnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do', soft-mutated after a (mi a wnaf hynny) · also 'I will see to it, bring it about that' (mi a wnaf na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'I will see that he never gets me'); auxiliary (Y gymryt a wnaf 'I will take it')
inheu: inheu (innau) — I/mine, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun marking contrast (a'm kyuoeth inheu 'my realm, mine')
guas: guas (gwas) — lad, young man, servant; noun m. (guas ditheu 'a lad, you')
ieuengtit: ieuengtit (ieuenctid) — youth, early part; noun f. (yn ieuengtit y dyd 'in the youth of the day' = early morning)
trannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, base form
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
uynyd: mynyd (mynydd) — mountain, upward; noun m. used adverbially 'upward', soft-mutated after y (a gyuodes y uynyd 'rose up')
penn: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., base form (Penn Annwuyn 'Head of Annwfn')
uchaf: uchaf (uchaf) — highest, uppermost; superlative of uchel 'high' (yn y lle uchaf 'in the highest place'); follows its noun, radical
geuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y geuyn attei 'and his back to her')
ymgueiraw: ymgyweiraw — to make oneself ready, settle oneself; reflexive verbal noun, ym- + kyweiraw 'prepare, set in order', written ymgueiraw (ymgueiraw yn y gyfrwy 'settling himself in his saddle') · also ymgueiraw ar 'to equip oneself with, get together' (ymgueiraw ar y ganuet marchauc 'to get ready with his hundred horsemen'); the sense with ar is uncertain
ueirch: march (march) — horse; plural meirch; soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive dy 'your' (dy ueirch 'your horses') · also soft after y 'his' (y ueirch 'his horses')
pryt: pryt (pryd) — form, appearance; noun m. (pryt ac ansawd 'form and appearance') · also 'time, hour, mealtime' (o'r pryt pwy gilyd 'from one hour to the next', sense approximate)
rith: rith (rhith) — shape, form, guise; noun m. (byd di i'm rith yno 'be there in my shape')
deu: deu (dau) — two (m.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following noun (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
ieueinc: ieuanc (ifanc) — young; plural form (gueisson ieueinc 'young lads')
eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
dos: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 sg. imperative 'go!' (dos y'r llys 'go to the court'; dos ragot 'go on')
ymywn: y mywn (mewn) — in, inside; preposition, the old y + mywn (ymywn ty 'inside a house'); no mutation
dywet: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. imperative 'say!' (Dywet titheu 'you say')
beird: bardd (bardd) — poet, bard; plural beird 'poets' (yn rith beird 'in the guise of poets'); radical
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
graessaw: graessaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m. (a graessaw wrthyt 'and welcome to you'); radical; modern croeso is the same word in a later form
wrthunt: wrth (wrth) + wynt — 'to, at, towards them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a uu wrthunt 'there was to them'); no mutation
gellwng: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 2 sg. imperative 'release!' (a gellwng y pryf hwnnw e ymdeith 'and release that creature'), though a verbal noun 'releasing' is possible (uncertain); g radical, as a 'and' gives only spirant mutation of c, p, t
mywn: y mywn (i mewn) — in, inside; adverbial phrase (yn dyuot y mywn 'coming in') · also prepositional 'in' (y mywn gogof 'in a cave')
diruawr: diruawr (dirfawr) — immense, vast, exceeding; adjective (diruawr llywenyd 'immense joy'); no mutation
herbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — meeting; in yn y herbyn 'to meet her', with h- before the vowel after y 'her' · also yn eu herbyn 'to meet them', with h- after eu 'their'
yneuad: neuad (neuadd) — hall; noun f., spelt with prothetic y- (Y'r yneuad yd aethont 'into the hall they went'); no mutation
wwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; written wwyta for uwyta, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wwyta 'to eat'); listed as a slip, though the first w may simply be the w-letter for the v-sound; the Red Book has vwyta
aethpwyt: mynet (mynd) — to go; impersonal preterite 'was gone, one went' in -pwyt (yd aethpwyt e Iwerdon 'it was gone to Ireland, they went to Ireland'); radical after the particle yd
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
daruot: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished, happen; verbal noun, with y/i of the person (kynn daruot idaw ymgueiraw 'before he had finished making ready')
bwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; verbal noun, also 'eating, a meal' (gwedy y bwyta kyntaf 'after the first eating', the first sitting of a feast)
ymdidan: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, to converse; noun/verbal noun, base form (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth ef)
guydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (also spelt Wydyon, Gwydyon), Math's nephew; Guydyon with u for w; radical (after the particle y in heb y Guydyon 'said Gwydion')
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here · also 'news, tidings' (Pa chwedleu yssyd yma? 'what news is there here?')
chyuarwydyt: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, storytelling; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyuarwydyt 'and (with) a tale')
kyuarwyd: kyuarwyd (cyfarwydd) — guidance, direction, information; noun m. (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi) · also 'storyteller, one skilled in tales' (Gwydyon goreu kyuarwyd yn y byt 'Gwydion the best storyteller in the world')
amser: amser — time; noun m. (Amser a doeth udunt 'the time came to them')
chyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing, a drinking-feast; noun m., spirant-mutated after a (a chyuedach 'and carousing')
ystauell: ystauell (ystafell) — room, chamber; noun f. (na guas ystauell 'no chamber-servant')
udunt: y (i) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'to them' (Amser a doeth udunt e uynet e gyscu)
gyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y (y gyscu 'to sleep')
aethant: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. preterite 'they went' (yd aethant 'they went')
hir: hir (hir) — long; adjective (yn hir 'for a long time') · also the epithet in a name (Hychdwn Hir 'Hychdwn the Tall/Long')
gyuodes: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (a gyuodes y uynyd 'and rose up')
gelwis: galw (galw) — to call; 3 sg. preterite 'called' in -is (y gelwis Nyssyen … y mab attaw 'Nisien called the boy to him'); a>e by vowel affection; radical after the particle y
hut: hut (hud) — magic, illusion, enchantment; noun m. (ystyr hut 'a meaning of magic')
allu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m., softened as the subject after oes (nyt oes allu 'there is no power')
goleuhau: goleuhau (goleuo; GPC goleuhau) — to grow light, brighten, light up; verbal noun after yn (llyma yn goleuhau pob lle 'behold, every place growing light'); no mutation
utkyrn: utgorn (utgorn) — horn, trumpet; plural utkyrn (modern utgyrn); noun m., radical after the article r
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
taraw: taraw (taro) — to strike, hit; verbal noun, fronted before a wnai (taraw a wnai pob un dyrnawt 'each one would strike a blow')
erchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask, request, bid; verbal noun (y erchi it 'to ask of you')
ieuanc: ieuanc (ifanc) — young; adjective following its noun (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
morwyn: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden, girl; noun f. (teccaf morwyn 'the fairest maiden'; morwyn gystal 'so good a maiden'); no mutation (radical)
wyrda: gwyrda (gwyrda) — noblemen; noun pl., base form, gwyr 'men' + da 'good' (A wyrda, heb ef) · also soft after o 'of' (a chan hynn o wyrda 'and with these noblemen', literally 'of noblemen')
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as a verbal noun directly after the verb (ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer 'they marvelled to see the fort')
gilyd: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; variant spelling of gilid (ar y gilyd 'against the other') · also pwy gilyd 'each (to) the other, one another' (o'r pryt pwy gilyd), soft-mutated after pwy; sense of pwy here uncertain
maent: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (y maent yn lluossauc 'they are numerous'); no mutation
tir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m. (dylyedauc tir a dayar 'a lord of land and earth')
gyntaf: kyntaf (cyntaf) — first; superlative, soft-mutated after y (ar y gossot kyntaf 'at the first onset') · also adverbial 'fastest, soonest' (ual y gallei gyntaf 'as fast as he could') · also soft after a feminine noun (y nos gyntaf 'the first night') · soft after yn, 'first, at first' (iawn y ti yn gyntaf 'redress to you first'; yn gyntaf ny doethant wy 'at first they did not come')
wnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall make' (ni a wnawn yr oet 'we shall make the appointment'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
in: y (i) + ni — 'to us, for us'; conjugated preposition 1 pl., spelt in (ys guell in 'it is better for us'); no mutation
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel')
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me') · also 'except, but' (un dyn yma onyt pedwar dyn 'one man here except four men')
caeu: caeu (cau) — to shut, close; verbal noun (yn gyflym caeu y got 'quickly shutting the bag')
arnam: ar (ar) + ni — 'on us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl. (drwc arnam 'harm on us'); no mutation
oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best') · also soft-mutated (g lost) after yn (yn oreu yn y byt 'best in the world')
dalho: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) repay' (Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you'), written with h before the ending (008 has dalo); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a
ywch: y (i) + chwi — 'to you'; conjugated preposition, 2 pl. (rodo da ywch 'may he give good to you'); no mutation · bot (bod) — to be; 2 pl. present 'you are' (canys ywch yn rwymedigaeth 'since you are in bondage'; yd ywch yn eu rith 'you are in their shape')
chwitheu: chwi (chwi) — you, for your part; conjunctive 2 pl. pronoun, 'you also' (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also'); no mutation
gwisc: gwisc (gwisg) — garment, dress; noun f. (gwisc hela 'hunting dress')
morynyon: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden, girl; plural morynyon (modern morynion); radical after the article y with a plural
odorun: godorun (uncertain) — a noise, disturbance, commotion (sense inferred from the dogs baying around it); noun m., here with g lost by soft mutation as the object after the verb (y clywei odorun 'he heard a disturbance'); the word is rare, sense uncertain
gwyr: gwr (gŵr) — men; noun pl. (kymryt gwrogaeth y gwyr 'taking the homage of the men') · also gwyr 3 sg. present of gwybot 'knows' (onys gwyr Branwen 'unless Branwen knows it')
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
guiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, put on armour, arm; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethant (guiscaw a wnaethant wynteu 'they armed themselves'); radical (gu- = gw-)
amdanaw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.); clothing/objects are 'about' a person (gwisc ... amdanaw)
derw: daruot (darfod) — to happen; derw = deryw, the old 3 sg. perfect 'it has happened' (a chan derw yt dywedut 'and since it has befallen you to say'); the Red Book also writes derw
wiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, clothe; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wiscaw eurwisc) · also soft after an object of erchi (erchwch y wyr y llys wiscaw amdanunt 'bid the men of the court put on gear about them') · also soft as the subject of daroed (Caswallawn a daroed idaw wiscaw llen hut 'Caswallon had put on a mantle of magic', literally 'putting on … had befallen him')
deryw: daruot (darfod) — to end, be over, come to pass; 3 sg. present with perfect sense, 'has ended, is over' (Ar ny deryw o'r wled 'what is not finished of the feast'); softened after ny, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show · also 'has happened, has befallen' (pa deryw ytti 'what has befallen you?'; yr hynn a deryw ymi 'what has befallen me')
neu: neu (neu) — (1) 'or' (kymriw neu archolleu 'injury or wounds'; neu ynteu 'or else'); (2) the affirmative particle neu 'lo, indeed' before a verb, neut before a vowel, neur with infixed 'r (see neut, neir)
reit: reit (rhaid) — need, necessity; noun m./f. (reit ymi 'need to me' = 'I need')
och: och (och) — alas; interjection of dismay (Och! heb y Riannon 'Alas, said Rhiannon')
paham: paham (pam) — why?; interrogative adverb, pa + am 'for what'
llyna: llyna (dyna) — there is, behold that; presentative particle, distal counterpart of llyma
llynghes: llynghes (llynges) — fleet; noun f. (a llynghes y gyt ac ef 'and a fleet together with him'); no mutation
yng: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yng before k (yng kyuyl y llys 'in the vicinity of the court'); the ng is the nasal mutation of the following c written on the preposition
kylch: kylch (cylch) — circle, ring, surrounding; noun m. (yn eu kylch 'around them'; yg kylch y ty 'around the house'); no mutation
ty: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m. (yn y ty yd oed cassec 'in the house was a mare'); no mutation · also 'you', emphatic 2 sg. pronoun after the verb (yd wyt ty yndaw 'you are in it')
dygyuor: dygyuor (dygyfor) — to muster, rally (a hunt); verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor yr hela 'beginning to muster the hunt') · also noun 'muster, gathering' (Dygyuor y wlat a doeth attunt 'the muster of the land came to them')
honei: o (o) + hi — conjugated preposition 3 sg. fem. 'of her, from her/it' (modern ohoni), written o honei; here 'from it' of the court, feminine llys (o honei y dechreuit pob anryded 'from it every honour was begun')
geissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun in -aw (ar geissaw eu llad 'on seeking to kill them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on'
diolwch: diolwch (diolch) — to thank; verbal noun/imperative-like (diolwch y'r gwr 'thank the man') · also noun 'thanks, gratitude' (diolwch ac elwissen 'thanks and alms-merit')
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
allei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/she could' (hyt na allei dywedut 'so that he could not speak'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na
colli: colli (colli) — to lose; verbal noun (wedy eu colli 'lost', lit. 'after their losing'; yn colli 'losing'); radical after eu and after the yn of the progressive
eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend')
cantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', the main administrative division of medieval Wales; noun m. (seith cantref Dyuet 'the seven cantrefs of Dyfed')
hediw: heddiw (heddiw) — today; adverb (na ommed neb hediw 'let no one be refused today')
uyth: byth (byth) — ever; with a negative, 'never'; adverb, soft-mutated (b>u) when used adverbially after the verb (dywedy di uyth 'you ever say'; na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'that he may never get me'; a uyd llawn dy got uyth 'will your bag ever be full')
dayar: dayar (daear) — earth, land; noun f. (am dir a dayar 'about land and earth')
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
awr: awr (awr) — hour; noun f. (hyt yr awr hon 'until this hour'); no mutation (vowel)
uuost: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were, you have been', soft-mutated after the perfective particle ry (ry uuost ti)
eiroet: eiroet (erioed) — ever, always (of the past); adverb (a welsei eiroet 'that he had ever seen')
dylyei: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, deserve; 3 sg. imperfect, negated 'would not deserve' (ual nas dylyei 'such that it would not deserve it') · also positive 'ought' (y rann a dylyei uot am y hwyneb 'the part that ought to be about her face')
borth: porth (porth) — help, protection, defender; noun m., a different word from porth 'gate' (bot yn borth y'r pryf 'to be protector for the creature'); soft-mutated (p>b) after predicative yn
kynt: kynt (cynt) — sooner, faster; comparative of buan 'swift' (nyt kynt … noc … 'no sooner … than'); also 'before, formerly'
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
math: Math — personal name: Math son of Mathonwy, lord of Gwynedd (Math uab Mathonwy oed arglwyd ar Wyned 'Math son of Mathonwy was lord over Gwynedd'); radical here (soft form Uath is separate)
mathonwy: Mathonwy — personal name, the father of Math (Math uab Mathonwy); genitive in a patronymic, no mutation
byt: byt (byd) — world; noun m. (o helgwn y byt 'of the hunting dogs of the world')
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour') · also 'from' after verbs of saving (waret rac hynn 'to deliver from this')
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
oc: o (o) — 'of, from', spelt oc before a vowel (oc eu hanuod 'against their will'); no mutation
lledrith: lledrith (lledrith) — illusion, enchantment, shape-changing; noun m. (yr hut a'r lledrith 'the enchantment and the illusion'); radical after the article 'r; also spelt lletrith
yndaw: yn (yn) + ef — conjugated preposition 'in him' (angheuawl dyrnawt yndaw ynteu; yssyd yndaw ef)
delediwhaf: telediw (no modern form) — handsome, comely; superlative delediwhaf 'handsomest' (yny oed delediwhaf gwass 'until he was the handsomest youth'); soft-mutated (t>d) as the complement directly after oed
welas: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. preterite 'saw', soft-mutated after relative y (yny welas y llys a'r kyuanned) · also soft after the particle a (Porth y gaer a welas 'the gate of the fort she saw') and after pan 'when' (Pann welas Kicua 'when Cigfa saw')
kymeryssant: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 pl. preterite 'they took' in -yssant (y kymeryssant wy ganheat 'they took leave'); radical after y
deccaf: teccaf (tecaf) — superlative of tec 'fair', soft-mutated after the feminine noun (y wreic deccaf 'the fairest woman')
bedydyaw: bedydyaw (bedyddio) — to baptize; verbal noun (Peri a wnaethont bedydyaw y mab 'they had the boy baptized'); no mutation
bedyd: bedyd (bedydd) — baptism; noun m. (o'r bedyd a wneit yna 'with the baptism that was done then'); no mutation after the article r
wneynt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would do', soft-mutated after a (kyuarch guell a wneynt idaw)
arnei: ar — conjugated preposition 'on her' (a charyat arnei 'and love on her') · also 'on it', of a feminine noun (a eistedo arnei 'who may sit on it', of the mound)
kyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, base form (yd wyt yn kyscu heno 'you are to sleep tonight')
wled: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f., soft-mutated after the article y as a feminine noun (y wled 'the feast'; y wled honno 'that feast')
hawd: hawd (hawdd) — easy; adjective (nat hawd genhyf i 'it is not easy with me'); no mutation (h-)
gyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, dominion; noun m., soft-mutated after y/a 'his' (y gyuoeth 'his realm') · also soft after o 'of' (o gyuoeth 'of realm') and as the object of a verb (phei mynhut gyuoeth 'if you wanted a realm')
rodaf: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give/put' (mi a'th rodaf di)
goreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good' (Goreu yw gennyf 'it is best with me' = I prefer)
gael: caffael (cael) — to get, have; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'its' (beichogi … y gael 'pregnancy, its getting' = to conceive)
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
ardudwy: Proper name — Ardudwy, the cantref in north-west Wales in which Harlech stands; no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
lys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (parth a'y lys) · also soft after prif 'chief', which softens the noun it precedes (prif lys 'chief court')
yg: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yg before a g: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg gwyd = yng ngwyd 'in the presence of'; yg got = yng nghod 'in a bag', with c>ngh after yn 'in') · also before k-: yg kylch y ty 'around the house' (yng nghylch), the g being the trace of the nasal mutation (c>ngh)
gwledychwys: gwledychu (gwledychu) — to rule, reign; 3 sg. preterite 'ruled' (Ac y gwledychwys ynteu Pryderi seith cantref Dyuet 'and Pryderi ruled the seven cantrefs of Dyfed'), -wys; no mutation after the particle y
phawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun (a phawb o'r guyrda 'and everyone of the nobles'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
arglwydiaeth: arglwydiaeth (arglwyddiaeth) — lordship, rule; noun f. (y arglwydiaeth ef 'his lordship')
